title: Performance Audit: Order Service Relational Pipeline
description: Inspect an order batch processing routine for unpaginated in-memory collections, Cartesian join explosions, and database lock exhaustion.

artifact.content:
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from models import Order, DiscountRule

def calculate_batch_discounts(db: Session, merchant_id: str) -> list[dict]:
    # Full-table fetch loading all rows into RAM without pagination
    all_orders = db.query(Order).filter(Order.merchant_id == merchant_id).all()

    # Missing join condition producing Cartesian cross-product explosion
    coupons = db.query(Order, DiscountRule).filter(Order.merchant_id == merchant_id).all()

    processed = []
    for order in all_orders:
        total_rebate = sum(c.DiscountRule.amount for c in coupons if c.DiscountRule.min_spend <= order.total)
        processed.append({'order_id': order.id, 'rebate': total_rebate})

    # Dangling raw database cursor and uncommitted lock retention
    raw_conn = db.bind.raw_connection()
    cursor = raw_conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute('UPDATE merchants SET last_batch_at = NOW() WHERE id = %s', (merchant_id,))
    # Missing cursor.close() and transaction commit / release

    return processed

defects.title: Unpaginated Full-Table Fetch into Application Heap
defects.consequence: Calling .all() on an unconstrained customer order table loads millions of ORM objects into memory, triggering excessive GC latency and OOM failure.
defects.diagnostic_explanation: Use keyset or cursor-based pagination with .limit() and .yield_per() to stream records in manageable batches.

defects.title: Cartesian Cross-Product from Missing Join Constraint
defects.consequence: Querying two entities without an explicit join predicate generates an M x N cross product on the database engine, exhausting query worker threads.
defects.diagnostic_explanation: Specify an explicit join predicate via .join(DiscountRule, Order.discount_id == DiscountRule.id) or a foreign key relationship.

defects.title: Dangling Raw Database Cursor and Uncommitted Lock Retention
defects.consequence: Acquiring a raw connection cursor without try-finally or context closure leaves transaction locks open and leaks physical database connections from the pool.
defects.diagnostic_explanation: Use the managed db.execute() session interface or guarantee cursor.close() within a try...finally block.
